extracted.intended_audience: Marine Corps and DoD contracting officers, acquisition/program managers, and policymakers involved in OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Thesis-level guidance and recommendations on applying OMB Circular A-76 to DoD/Marine Corps competitive sourcing (outsourcing) of installation support services, including required steps, risks, program management, definitions, and appendices of commercial and inherently governmental activities. Aimed at helping contracting officers manage A-76 studies effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 study required steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular describes the steps that must be taken in an A-76 study, to include: Development of a Performance Work Statement; Conduct of a Management study to develop the Government's Most Efficient Organization; Development of the in-house Government cost estimate; Conduct of a Cost Comparison between the MEO and lowest priced responsible and responsive bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four steps are presented as the procedural backbone of an A-76 study and should be followed in sequence. The Cost Comparison must follow the principles and procedures of the Circular and Supplement to assure equity. Failure to follow these steps correctly can lead to protests and invalid comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) quality and comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: "The development of a sound and comprehensive Performance Work Statement ranks at the top of the list." A PWS is a statement of the technical, functional and performance characteristics of the work to be performed; identifies essential functions; determines performance factors including location, units of work, quantity of work units, and the quality and timeliness of the work units; serves as the scope of work and basis for all costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete PWS is critical — omissions (not capturing all work currently performed by the Government) are a principal risk and can negate anticipated savings when work is later added by contract modification. The thesis stresses PWS development as the single most important element dictating success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of competition and cost-comparison compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers must operate within the boundaries established in OMB Circular A-76, and the solicitation and source selection plan when conducting competitions and cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to conduct cost comparisons and competitions within stated guidelines will almost certainly result in protests. Ensure adherence to the Circular's procedures and the source selection documentation; document decisions and follow prescribed equity and comparison rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan and Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan outlines the changes that will result in the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) to perform a commercial activity in-house. The MEO is the product of the Management Plan and is based upon the Performance Work Statement (PWS); it is the basis for all Government costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Management Plan should provide staffing patterns and operating procedures serving as baseline for in-house cost estimates. The MEO must be realistic and traceable to the PWS to produce an equitable cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and conflict-of-interest controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officials must ensure that personnel who may have a conflict of interest are prohibited from sitting on source selection boards or technical evaluation teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper manning of the A-76 team is essential. Conflicted personnel on evaluation bodies undermine integrity and increase protest risk. Implement clear conflict screening and replacement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management: identify and manage A-76-specific risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting community is inconsistently applying the risk management process to A-76 studies; many commands failed to identify risks originating from the A-76 process and often focused only on Government employee reactions rather than the full range of risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands should comprehensively identify risks (e.g., PWS omissions, inappropriate contract type, unauthorized changes by on-site personnel), assess their impact, and apply mitigation strategies. Risk management must be applied consistently across the contracting community to avoid schedule slippage and lost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program management approach and assignment of an A-76 program manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, Installation Commanders should adopt a program management approach for the conduct of A-76 studies: designate a program manager and empower that person with broad authority. Establishment of a quasi program office for A-76 studies would establish unity of command and a focused group leader for A-76 efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program managers should mirror processes used for major weapon systems where appropriate; they should have sole authority to approve deviations from the study schedule, identify and mitigate risks, and be accountable for successes and failures. Integrated product teams alone are helpful but not sufficient without a program manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish study timelines, program metrics, and earned value tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers should focus on metrics involved in tracking the progress of the commercial study: establish study timelines, program metrics for tracking progress, and retain sole authority to approve deviations from the study schedule. An example of a tracking method is a modified Earned Value Management System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define measurable milestones and use objective tracking (e.g., EVM-style metrics) to detect schedule/budget slippage early. Metrics should be tied to deliverables (PWS milestones, management-plan tasks) and reported to leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized database of best practices and lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Defense should establish a database accessible through the Internet containing information on lessons learned from completed A-76 studies. The database should be resident within the Acquisition Web homepage and Services should be required to submit input at the end of each completed study. The primary focus should be A-76 study management and contracting issues, including lessons learned and best practices on developing Performance Work Statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A centralized repository addresses the current dispersion and incompleteness of information across the Web and commands; it enables institutional learning and reduces repeated mistakes across Services and installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver procedures for mission-critical commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Waiver procedures to OMB A-76 should be established which installation commanders can use to protect commercial activities they deem mission critical. This allows installation commanders to tailor competitive sourcing studies to current conditions and retain flexibility in commercial determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers provide a mechanism to protect essential mission performance where strict application of A-76 would be counterproductive. Procedures should be standardized so waivers are defensible and consistent with law (e.g., FAIR Act) while allowing local tailoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and use of past performance and evaluation for best overall value
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 should be changed to define practices for capturing cost and past performance data on commercial activities currently performed by Government employees. The changes should allow for incorporation of past performance data into evaluation criteria for making a contract award. Contracting officers should be given latitude to evaluate competitor past performance, technical approaches, management plans and other relevant factors and be allowed to award contracts to organization capable of providing the best overall value to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect data similar to what is collected on commercial firms; permit source selection that considers best value rather than only lowest price in appropriate circumstances, subject to legal and Circular constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-MEO performance review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When services are performed in-house as a result of a cost comparison, a formal review and inspection of the Most Efficient Organization (MEO) should be conducted, typically following the end of the first full year of performance. Post-MEO Performance Reviews confirm that the MEO has been implemented in accordance with the Transition, establish the MEO's ability to perform the services of the PWS and confirm that actual costs are within the estimates contained in the in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct systematic post-implementation audits to verify performance and cost assumptions; adjust for formal mission or scope-of-work changes. Use findings to inform lessons learned and database entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measures and performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance measures provide indicators, expressed in qualitative, quantitative or other tangible terms, that indicate whether current performance is reasonable and cost effective (e.g., workload and output-to-cost ratios, error rates, timeliness measures, user satisfaction). A performance standard reflects the minimum, sector-specific, Federal requirement for the performance of a commercial activity and incorporates both quality measures and cost measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear, measurable metrics in the PWS and Management Plan to enable objective comparisons. Ensure cost measures reflect the Circular's comparability procedures so industry and in-house performance are measured equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Surveillance is the method by which Federal employees will supervise in-house or contract performance to ensure that the standards of the PWS are met within the costs bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement surveillance plans that specify inspection, monitoring, and acceptance criteria tied to PWS standards and contract payment/incentive structures. QA activities are distinct from contract administration and should align with performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions: retention criteria and list
rubrics_metrics.description: An inherently governmental activity is one that is so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Federal employees; activities meeting these criteria are not subject to Circular A-76 or this Supplement. Appendix C lists examples (e.g., control of prosecutions and adjudicatory functions; command of military forces; conduct of foreign relations; determination of agency policy; selection/approval/award/administering of prime contracts; approval of FOIA responses; licensing/inspections; control of treasury accounts, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed functions and criteria to screen activities for exclusion from competitive sourcing. Consult OFPP Policy Letter 92-1 for additional guidance about avoiding unacceptable transfer of official responsibility to contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption determination
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption is a determination, made in accordance with Circular A-76 and this Supplement, that a commercial activity may be converted to or from in-house, contract or ISSA performance, without cost comparison and may be justified by reasons other than cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and document the rationale for exemptions clearly and in accordance with the Circular to ensure defensibility and to avoid improper bypassing of required cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and identification of commercial activities (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A commercial activity is the process resulting in a product or service that is or could be obtained from a private sector source. Appendix B provides extensive examples of commercial activities adapted from OMB Circular A-76 (e.g., audiovisual services, ADP services, food services, health services, industrial shops, maintenance/repair/testing, management support services, manufacturing, office/admin services, printing, real property, security, systems engineering, transportation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories and examples to classify functions under study. The breadth of listed activities demonstrates typical areas subject to competitive sourcing and helps identify comparable commercial benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison definition and equity procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost comparison is the process whereby the estimated cost of Government performance of a commercial activity is formally compared, in accordance with the principles and procedures of this Circular and Supplement, to the cost of performance by commercial or ISSA sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that comparisons follow the Circular's procedures for equity (e.g., inclusion of overhead, comparable cost bases, allocation rules). Properly document assumptions, labor/hours, and overhead to withstand protest and audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder communication to mitigate risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The management of identified risks depends on communication between the contracting officer, A-76 program office, installation commander and the customer. Each must understand the needs and goals of each of the stakeholders to comprehend the impact of all decisions made in relation to competitive sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster open communication channels among stakeholders throughout the study to reduce misunderstandings, prevent unauthorized contract changes, and improve implementation. Document stakeholder decisions and rationale to support transparency.
